detail.measured: 2026-10-10, seat-102, branch kernels-search, P1's speedcheck.py (device clock, interleaved A/B, 3 rounds). Matmul 13:25; RMSNorm and copy at the 2048-token timing shapes 13:55.
detail.times_are: the sum over each op's time_shapes in shapes.py, the same sum the referee's speedup uses

matmul.expert: kernels/matmul_expert.py: AWS's SDK 2.32 fully optimised tutorial matmul, accumulating K-blocks in fp32. Correct on 8 chip shapes, worst 0.50 bf16 ulps.
matmul.expert_as_published: kernels/matmul_expert_aws.py: same kernel with AWS's bf16 K-block accumulation. Referee verdict WRONG: 5.3 bf16 ulps at K=2048 (limit 4).
matmul.floor: not measured: no matmul floor is claimed

rmsnorm.floor: kernels/copy_floor.py: the same bytes copied through SBUF, rows packed into partitions in >= 2 overlapping chunks. Against the one-tile-per-DMA copy (kernels/copy_tiled.py): 89.7 vs 91.3 us at 2048x4096, 51.1 vs 344.2 us at 32768x128 (256-byte rows).
rmsnorm.room: start / floor = 1.82x at input_layernorm, 6.95x at q_norm, 3.68x on the sum

history_256_tokens.why_replaced: at 256 tokens a 4 MiB copy took ~20 us, mostly the ~17 us launch cost
